records.section: Case Study: State v. Benjamin Allen
records.text: Case Study: State v. Benjamin Allen A military veteran and father was accused of sexual assault in Lee County, North Carolina, in October 2019. The prosecution that followed lasted more than six years. This page documents what the record shows and how the case continued despite evidence that contradicted the charge at every structural level. Profiles of the people involved are on the Players page.

records.title: Case Study: Wrongful Accusation | State v. Benjamin Allen
records.text: Timeline of Impossibility The departure from Schooly’s bar was marked by a fundamental contradiction between witness testimony and the objective surveillance record. Lauren Deal’s sworn testimony portrayed the departure as a coordinated group event designed to establish the State’s “position of trust” theory. The video evidence shows otherwise: they did not leave together. That single fact renders this portion of her testimony highly suspect, and the problems compound from there across every time anchor that follows. TWO-COL: NARRATIVE + TRANSCRIPT State’s Theory Group of four (Deal, Allen, DeMarco, Happel) remained together at closing and departed together in Allen's white truck. Deal was comfortably familiar with the vehicle and the group. The departure served as the foundation for the “position of trust” aggravator. The testimony given to support this false narrative is as manufactured as the aggravating factor the ADA improperly applied to the charge. Video Reality The surveillance footage shows they did not leave together — departures occurred at separate times. Because Deal left the bar independently, the alleged joint-departure conversation about DeMarco driving and whose truck it was could not have taken place as described. Carmen Love also confirmed to Detective Freeman that the evening did not unfold the way Deal described to law enforcement but later changed her story when she was informed what the narrative would be for that evening. ⚖ Prosecution Exchange — Trial Transcript MS. BARTHOLOMEW: “Did you ever fall down while you were at Schooly’s? And when it became time to leave with Ben, Joseph, and Steve, what type of vehicle did you guys get into?” LAUREN DEAL: “A white lifted truck.” MS. BARTHOLOMEW: “How do you know it was Ben’s truck?” LAUREN DEAL: “I had seen it before, and he made the comment on the way out that Jay was going to drive his truck because he was the least intoxicated of all of us.” The truck was stock — not lifted. The “prior familiarity” claim is inconsistent with a timeline showing no meaningful contact for years. The designated-driver arrangement was Allen’s, made before Deal arrived; he did not describe DeMarco as “least intoxicated.” The detail in the complete fabrication here is striking. The video shows Deal leaving separately. There is no disputing that fact. There isn't even a close following of individual that could have led her to be mistaken. It is just entirely made up to push a narative. TIME ANCHORS ⏰ Video-Confirmed & Documented Time Anchors (After hours of video that directly contradicts the evening described by Lauren Deal) ~2:00 AM Bar closes; lights on. Deal testified the group was together at this point. 2:04 AM DeMarco seen on video retrieving sandals at Schooly’s (objective video anchor). 2:25–2:35 AM Group estimated to arrive at Allen’s residence, based on ~15-minute drive time. ~2:40 AM Estimated exit — if Happel’s “less than five minutes” window is accepted at face value. 3:42 AM Deal arrives at CCH — State’s Exhibit 1 Video (objective anchor). 5:23 AM Chapel Hill intake paperwork. Teresa Deal testified the drive took approximately 45 minutes. HAPPEL 5-MIN + ESCAPE NARRATIVE The Five-Minute Impossibility Happel placed the entire period from entry to exit at less than five minutes . Within that window, the State’s account requires all of the following to have occurred: Entering the house and unlocking the door Using the bathroom Redressing after bathroom use An alleged push onto a 36-inch-high bed A one-handed overhead restraint of a resisting adult Removal of clothing from two adults The assault itself Escape from the residence That sequence is not merely tight. It is facially implausible. The Escape Narrative — Terrain & Light Claimed Ran hysterically through dense woods in pitch-black darkness for nearly an hour, sustaining briar cuts. No pants, no shoes. Screamed that Allen was “the devil” and that Happel and DeMarco “work for him.” Contradicted by the Record The route she identified leads onto an open airfield , not dense forest. No briars exist along that path; her cuts do not resemble briar injuries. Astronomical data: approximately 70% lunar illumination that night — directly contradicts the claim she could not see her hand in front of her face. DeMarco said he saw her running through a field . Deal said she was hiding behind a tree . The witnesses contradict each other as to her location. The direction she claimed to have run was the opposite direction of the road she said she ran toward and claimed she was located on 🧠 Interactive Mindmap: Explore the complete branch structure in Deconstructing the Lauren Deal Narrative to examine environmental conditions, terrain contradictions, and physiological implausibility. THREE GAP CALLOUTS ⚠ Unaccounted Time: Three Irreconcilable Gaps Gap 1 — Exit to CCH ∼62 min From ∼2:40 AM exit to 3:42 AM CCH arrival. DeMarco and Happel claimed they searched only five minutes before DeMarco drove off. Where were Deal and DeMarco for the rest of the hour? Her visible impairment, her obesity, lack of physical fitness, and lack of footwear make a prolonged solo run implausible. Gap 2 — CCH to Chapel Hill ∼56 min unaccounted CCH arrival 3:42 AM. Chapel Hill intake 5:23 AM. Teresa Deal testified the drive took ∼45 minutes — accounting for 45 of 101 elapsed minutes. The remaining 56 minutes at CCH are unexplained. No CCH report to law enforcement has been produced, as would be required in a sexual assault case. Gap 3 — The Girlfriend Problem 45+ min round trip DeMarco called his girlfriend in Fayetteville. Deal was later wearing the sweatpants the girlfriend brought to CCH. The drive from Fayetteville alone takes at least 45 minutes . The claim that they arrived at CCH and immediately turned around for Chapel Hill cannot be true. POSITION OF TRUST COLLAPSE State’s “Position of Trust” Theory vs. Surveillance Record State’s Claim Allen occupied a position of trust that he exploited to lure Deal—evidenced by her recognizing his truck from previous occasions, greeting him with a hug, and entrusting him with her keys. Implied Warrant A woman who hands over her keys and joins a familiar male friend’s group for a social gathering acts under the umbrella of established trust, which can constitute a statutory aggravator. Video Disproof Allen refused the keys ; Deal handed them to DeMarco — a man she had never met. Deal’s friends left earlier. She eventually left the bar alone after multiple failed attempts to get Allen’s attention. It was not a smooth group departure. The State needed that cohesion because it was the social glue for the “lure” theory. SYNTHESIS Pattern: Narrative Manufacture The account of who remained at the bar, who left with whom, how the truck was identified, why DeMarco drove, how intoxicated Deal was, and what happened after leaving the residence seriously conflicts with the video, timelines, terrain, and common sense. None of this appears ambiguous. Much of it is directly testable. Deal’s trial testimony diverged sharply from her earlier statements. The later testimony became cleaner, more element-driven, and more useful to the prosecution. That pattern does not look like natural memory development. When the polished version directly conflicts with objective video evidence, the problem is no longer mere inconsistency — it becomes evidence of narrative manufacture . Carmen Love told Freeman that the evening did not unfold as Deal described to law enforcement. Rather than preserving those contradictions, he altered the official narrative to bury them.

records.section: 1. The Initial Complaint: What Was Alleged, When, and to Whom
records.text: 1. The Initial Complaint: What Was Alleged, When, and to Whom The complaint arose from events at Schooly’s bar in Lee County, North Carolina, in the early hours of October 19, 2019, and the hours that followed. The sequence below draws on the documentary record, testimony, and video evidence now available in this archive. The Bar — Evening of October 18 into October 19, 2019 Lauren Deal and her group arrived at Goodfellas around 6:30 p.m. on October 18, 2019, and at Schooly’s around 9:30 p.m. Benjamin Allen and his group arrived at Schooly’s at approximately 12:08 a.m. on October 19. The bar video is part of this archive. That video shows Deal's group and Allen's group present simultaneously. It also shows specific interactions — including Deal initiating contact with Allen, attempting to introduce him to others, and following him after he walked away — that directly contradict key elements of the later complaint. The Allegation Deal alleged that Allen sexually assaulted her after she accompanied him from the bar. She alleged she escaped by running through pitch-black darkness and briars, hid behind trees, and was eventually spotted from the road by Joe DeMarco, who picked her up. She described the environment as “complete darkness” yet still identified vehicle types, recognized DeMarco by sight, and maintained eye contact as she approached his vehicle. First Report — Officer Isaac Haines Officer Haines conducted the first institutional interview with Deal. He testified that his role was preliminary fact-finding to determine whether the matter warranted a detective assignment. This framing creates a timing problem: Freeman testified that he had already been notified about a sexual assault allegation before the Haines interview was complete, suggesting the matter was escalated to detective-level investigation before the threshold predicate had been established. Haines described the investigative mission as proving Allen guilty, not determining whether the allegation was credible. Haines was subsequently promoted to Detective following this case.
keywords: 1. The Initial Complaint: What Was Alleged, When, and to Whom

records.section: 2. The Investigation Record: What Was Collected vs. What Was Ignored
records.text: 2. The Investigation Record: What Was Collected vs. What Was Ignored An investigation's integrity is measured not only by what it found but by what it chose not to look for. The omissions in this record are not minor. They are structural — the materials most likely to undermine the complaint are precisely the materials that were handled selectively or not at all. Collected Bar Video Footage Video from Schooly’s was collected. The footage documents Deal’s behavior and interactions that evening, including moments when Deal initiates contact with Allen—contradicting her later account—and shows Carmen Love and James Morrison leaving together without speaking to Allen or his friends, directly undermining the social context the investigation’s narrative claims. Not Collected / Not Used Statements from Material Witnesses James Morrison and Peter West III — both present at the bar and part of Deal’s extended social group — were never interviewed. Morrison was Carmen Love’s boyfriend. West’s father was a Sheriff’s Office employee who signed Allen’s jail release. The record provides no explanation for why two identified witnesses who were present for the relevant events were never contacted. Distorted Carmen Love's Initial Statement Love’s first recorded statement to Freeman — her own family member — did not identify Allen by name and did not supply the incriminating detail later attributed to it. Freeman subsequently recast that statement in official documents. Because the original recording exists and the defense can access it, the alteration is directly comparable and provable. Freeman claimed to have used Love’s statement as a basis for probable cause even though its actual content did not support that use. Uninvestigated The $150,000 Extortion Demand A $150,000 extortion demand connected to Joel Kelly preceded or accompanied the formal accusation. Kelly’s daughter was Deal’s best friend; Deal’s other best friend worked for Kelly. The investigation did not adequately explore the financial motive and social architecture of the extortion—a gap that would be highly relevant to any credibility assessment of the complainant’s motive. Manufactured Evidence Destruction Innuendo Freeman later suggested that cleanup behavior at Allen’s residence was consistent with evidence destruction—without processing the scene in any way that would establish what evidence existed there, where it was located, or whether anything had been removed. The insinuation extended to a different room from the one where the assault was allegedly committed. This is the investigative equivalent of creating a negative implication from the absence of something the investigation never actually looked for. Chronological Defect The Assignment Timing Problem The testimonial record indicates that Freeman was already aware of and involved in the case before Haines's preliminary interview was complete. If Haines's stated role was to determine whether a detective was needed, then Freeman's prior notification is a structural impossibility unless the escalation decision had been made before any factual basis for it existed. This creates a Franks v. Delaware concern: the chronology underlying the probable cause affidavit may be materially false.

records.text: 3. The Charging Decision A charging decision carries legal and moral weight. It requires a genuine assessment of whether the available evidence, taken at its strongest, could support a conviction before a fair finder of fact. The materials in this archive raise serious questions about whether this assessment was ever conducted honestly. What Existed at the Time of Charging A complainant whose account included physical impossibilities contradicted by terrain, lighting conditions, and recorded video. Bar video showing Deal initiating contact with Allen, tracking him after he walked away, and voluntarily accompanying his group. An initial witness statement (Carmen Love) that was exculpatory in its original form. An investigator with an undisclosed familial relationship to a key witness. Two identified material witnesses who had never been interviewed. An unexplained extortion demand in the same social circle as the complainant. A chronological impossibility in the escalation timeline that should have triggered review of the probable cause affidavit but no probable cause affidavit exist even after almost seven years. What the Decision Required The decision to charge over these materials required either that the prosecutor had not reviewed them, had reviewed them and concluded they were immaterial, or had reviewed them and concluded that conviction was achievable regardless of what they showed. The prosecution's subsequent conduct —including the handling of Exhibit 4, the aggravating-factor construction, and indicators of witness coaching — points to the third possibility.
keywords: 3. The Charging Decision

records.section: 4. Pressure Dynamics: Family Connections to Law Enforcement and Local DA Relationships
records.text: 4. Pressure Dynamics: Family Connections to Law Enforcement and Local DA Relationships The structural environment surrounding this case was not neutral. The record documents a set of relationships between the complainant’s social circle and law enforcement personnel that, taken together, explain how a case with this evidentiary profile was treated as credible, why certain witnesses disappeared from the record, and how the language attributed to insiders ("it didn’t matter whether Mr. Allen was innocent") reflects something more than personal bias. Freeman ↔ Carmen Love The lead investigator had a familial relationship with the key witness whose initial statement was exculpatory. The investigator recast Love’s statement rather than preserving it. This conflict was not disclosed. Under basic due process principles, an investigator with a family relationship to a witness cannot be treated as neutral when the question is whether that witness’s account corroborates or undermines the charge. Freeman ↔ James Morrison Morrison was Love’s boyfriend — and therefore connected to Freeman through Love. He was at the bar, and his non-interview is unexplained. Failing to interview him fits the broader pattern: the record excluded every uncontrolled witness who could have provided an independent account of Deal’s behavior that evening. Peter West III ↔ Sheriff's Office West was present at the bar. His father worked at the Sheriff’s Office and personally signed Allen’s jail release. West was never interviewed. His institutional proximity and absence from the investigation suggest the investigation’s scope was shaped—not by the evidence—but by the social and professional networks within it. Jolynda Adcock's Statement Adcock's documented statement — "it didn't matter whether Mr. Allen was innocent" — is not merely an expression of personal hostility. It is a statement about perceived institutional power. It reflects the understanding, within the complainant's extended circle, that the Sheriff's Department relationships available to them were sufficient to make the outcome of the case independent of its factual merits. Haines's Promotion Officer Haines, the initial responding officer who described the investigative mission as proving Allen guilty rather than determining the truth of the allegation, was subsequently promoted to Detective. Whatever the formal basis for that promotion, its timing in this case's institutional record is documented here. The Extortion Network The $150,000 extortion demand, connected to Joel Kelly, whose daughter was Deal’s best friend and whose employee was Deal’s other best friend, was generated before or alongside the formal complaint. The failure to investigate this network as a source of motive — and the failure to trace its relationship to the timing and substance of the allegation — is a fundamental investigative omission.

records.section: 5. Evidence That Contradicted the Narrative — and How It Was Handled
records.text: 5. Evidence That Contradicted the Narrative — and How It Was Handled The complaint's narrative is not merely weak at its edges. The core of it — the flight, the darkness, the geography — collapses under basic scrutiny. The following contradictions are documented in the record and cross-referenced in contradictions.html . The Darkness Claim vs. the Lunar Record Deal described running in "complete darkness." Photometric and radiometric data confirm approximately 70% lunar illumination (Waxing/Waning Gibbous) on the night in question. At this illumination level, a person with normal vision can detect large objects at distances exceeding 50 feet, recognize body silhouettes and movement, and navigate open terrain without artificial light. Deal simultaneously claimed "complete darkness" while identifying that an approaching vehicle was not Allen's large truck, recognizing DeMarco as the driver, establishing eye contact with him, and making a deliberate decision to approach. The word "darkness" is invoked selectively: it appears to explain disorientation and disappears when recognition, identification, and volitional conduct need to be established. The Geographic Impossibility Deal claimed to have run through woods and briars in the direction away from the house before reaching a road near Route 1. The direction she described leads to a large, flat, open airfield — not woods, not briars, not concealed terrain. There is no dense undergrowth in that direction. The airfield is open and visible. To reach the road near Route 1, she would have had to reverse course and run back toward the house. The investigation did not engage with this geographic contradiction. The terrain has been documented in the scene archive at scene.html . The Video Record vs. the Social Context Claimed Bar video shows Carmen Love and James Morrison departing Schooly's at approximately 12:41 AM — without having spoken to Allen or his group. Deal's account implied a different social context within the bar. The video shows Deal initiating contact with Allen, attempting to introduce him to others, and following him after he walked away. The video does not show a reluctant or passive witness. It shows voluntary engagement. That footage is timestamped and available in the archive. DeMarco's Statement vs. Deal's Trial Testimony Joe DeMarco told Freeman he saw Deal "running through a field near Route 1" while driving. Deal's trial testimony described running through pitch-black woods in a different direction. These accounts are not in minor tension — they describe different physical scenarios in different locations under different conditions. DeMarco's account was inaccurate from the beginning as he was afraid of getting accused of something by Deal so he went along with making up a story. His account was changed in Freeman's search warrant affidavit and retellings. Deal's trial account does not align with the geography and lighting conditions. Exhibit 4: The Facebook Messages Facebook messages identified as Exhibit 4 were presented without device metadata, custodial proof, or foundation sufficient to resolve attribution — particularly where later screenshots identified a different user of the same phone. The court conditionally admitted the exhibit subject to the State's obligation to link it to a prior conversation that would provide context. That condition was not meaningfully satisfied. Only the first screenshot was emphasized; subsequent screenshots identifying another phone user were withheld from the jury's view, in apparent violation of N.C. R. Evid. 106. How Contradictory Evidence Was Handled The documentary record reflects a consistent pattern: evidence that undermined the narrative was either ignored (Morrison, West), recast (Love's initial statement), managed selectively (Exhibit 4's full screenshot sequence), or met with insinuation rather than proof (the cleanup/destruction-of-evidence narrative). The pattern is too consistent to be explained by inadvertence. Each handling decision was in a direction that favored conviction.

records.section: 6. The Arc of the 6+ Year Prosecution
records.text: 6. The Arc of the 6+ Year Prosecution The prosecution of Benjamin Allen extended more than six years from the date of the alleged offense in October 2019. That duration is not simply a product of court congestion or procedural complexity. It reflects a sequence of decisions that prolonged exposure to prosecution for a defendant whose record contained, from the outset, materials that should have triggered review. Initial Arrest and Charge Allen was arrested and charged with sexual assault following the investigation led by Detective Freeman. The arrest took place despite the evidentiary defects described in this record: an uninvestigated extortion demand, an exculpatory witness statement that had been recast, two uninterviewed material witnesses, and a probable cause chronology that did not hold together. Continuances and Delay The case proceeded through hearings, continuances, and pretrial motions over an extended period. Each continuance that moved the trial date further into the future extended Allen's period of legal jeopardy — with consequences for employment, housing, family access, and health documented in the downstream harms section below. The full docket record is available in the document archive. Motions Practice Pretrial motions raised issues including Brady violations, the chronological defect in the probable cause affidavit (implicating Franks v. Delaware ), and evidentiary handling failures. The Exhibit 4 conditional admission ruling, in which the court required the State to link the exhibit to a prior conversation before relying on it, is a documented instance of the court placing conditions on the prosecution's evidence presentation — conditions the State then did not satisfy. Narrative Evolution as a Prosecution Tool Across the arc of the case, Deal's testimony evolved. The "position of trust" aggravating factor developed over time in ways inconsistent with the earliest statements and with the video record of Deal's behavior at the bar. That evolution — from a social encounter at a bar where Deal initiated contact, to a story in which Allen held a position of trust over Deal — required the original record to be progressively buried rather than resolved. The more the narrative evolved, the weaker its connection to the documented facts became.
keywords: 6. The Arc of the 6+ Year Prosecution

records.text: 7. Downstream Harms A prosecution does not exist only in courtrooms. It exists in every part of a person's life from the day of arrest forward. The following categories of harm document what a false accusation that proceeds for more than six years actually costs — not as a hypothetical, but as a record of documented consequence. Employment Career Destruction Allen lost employment as a direct consequence of the accusation and the protracted prosecution. Military service and the vocational record built before the accusation were effectively severed. Re-employment becomes structurally difficult for a defendant whose status remains unresolved across years of hearings and continuances. Housing Housing Instability Loss of employment and the financial burden of legal defense across more than six years produces housing instability. A defendant cannot plan housing, financing, or community stability when their legal status remains unresolved—with each continuance extending the period of uncertainty. Family Separation from Family Allen is a father. An accusation of this nature and duration does not only restrict the accused's freedom — it disrupts parental access, creates conditions for protective orders, and forces children to grow up with a parent under prosecution. That harm is not reversible by acquittal. Finances Legal and Financial Cost Defending a felony-level sexual assault case over six or more years — through motions, hearings, trial preparation, and any appellate proceedings — produces a financial cost that exceeds the resources of most individuals. That cost is borne entirely by the defendant while the State prosecutes with public resources. Health Physical and Psychological Toll Six years of pending felony prosecution — with its associated uncertainty, financial stress, social stigma, family disruption, and public record — produces documented psychological harm. For a military veteran who has already navigated service-related stress, the compounding effect of a fabricated accusation and institutional pursuit is not a marginal addition to a normal life. It is a consuming structural experience. Reputation The Public Record Problem An arrest and charge for sexual assault creates a public record. That record exists independent of outcome. Where the prosecution is false — built on a recast witness statement, uninvestigated exculpatory evidence, and a complainant whose account is physically impossible — the reputational harm is not a byproduct of a fair system. It is a harm produced by the system's failure.

records.text: 8. Comparison to Base Rates The question of how rare it is for a case with this evidentiary profile to proceed this far is not an idle one. Base rate data on false accusation rates, prosecution rates conditional on evidence quality, and case duration data provide the population-level context against which this record should be evaluated. The Evidence Profile of This Case Bar video directly contradicting the complainant's account of the social interaction. Documented physical impossibilities in the escape narrative (terrain, lighting, direction). An exculpatory witness statement that was altered rather than preserved. Two identified material witnesses who were never interviewed. An undisclosed conflict of interest in the lead investigator. A financial motive (extortion) that was not investigated. A probable cause chronology that contained a structural impossibility. A prosecution's evidence handling that violated multiple evidentiary rules. What Base Rates Suggest Research on sexual assault prosecution — including work by the National Registry of Exonerations and academic studies of prosecutorial screening — consistently finds that cases with exculpatory video evidence, physical impossibilities in the complainant's narrative, and undisclosed investigator conflicts rarely proceed past initial screening where those materials are meaningfully engaged. Cases in which those materials are present but suppressed, recast, or ignored present a different pattern: the materials that should have stopped the case become invisible to the decision-makers downstream, and the case proceeds on the momentum of the charge rather than the merits of the record. A 6+ year prosecution in the face of this evidentiary profile is an outlier. It is not explained by case complexity. It is explained by the structural dynamics documented in this archive: investigator conflicts, selective witness handling, and a complaint embedded in a network with direct access to law enforcement. The Research Context False allegation rates in sexual assault cases are contested in the academic literature, with credible estimates ranging from approximately 2% to 10% of reported cases depending on methodology. What is less contested is that the subset of false allegations that result in charges, trial, and multi-year prosecution represent a small fraction of even those cases. For a case with documented exculpatory video, physical geography inconsistencies, an uninvestigated financial motive, and an investigator conflict to reach trial — and proceed past trial — places this matter in the extreme tail of that already-small population. The data snapshot page provides additional context on these figures.

Cases in which those materials are present but suppressed, recast, or ignored present a different pattern: the materials that should have stopped the case become invisible to the decision-makers downstream, and the case proceeds on the momentum of the charge rather than the merits of the record. A 6+ year prosecution in the face of this evidentiary profile is an outlier. It is not explained by case complexity. It is explained by the structural dynamics documented in this archive: investigator conflicts, selective witness handling, and a complaint embedded in a network with direct access to law enforcement.

records.text: The Research Context False allegation rates in sexual assault cases are contested in the academic literature, with credible estimates ranging from approximately 2% to 10% of reported cases depending on methodology. What is less contested is that the subset of false allegations that result in charges, trial, and multi-year prosecution represent a small fraction of even those cases. For a case with documented exculpatory video, physical geography inconsistencies, an uninvestigated financial motive, and an investigator conflict to reach trial — and proceed past trial — places this matter in the extreme tail of that already-small population. records.section: How Long Can the Justice System Disrupt the Life of an Innocent Man?
records.text: How Long Can the Justice System Disrupt the Life of an Innocent Man? Two men, one Georgia jail, and more than a decade without a conviction. The Maurice Jimmerson Case (10 Years, 10 Months) The Arrest. Maurice Jimmerson was arrested in Dougherty County, Georgia, in May 2013 on murder charges. The Stagnation. He was held continuously in a local jail awaiting his day in court. His case was delayed for nearly eleven years due to systemic bureaucratic failures, a courthouse flood, the COVID-19 pandemic, and an eight-month stretch where the court completely forgot to assign him an attorney. The Zero-Conviction Conclusion. He finally went to trial in July 2023, which resulted in a mistrial (hung jury) rather than a conviction. Because he had spent over a decade locked up as a legally innocent man, his defense attorney successfully argued that a retrial would heavily violate his Sixth Amendment rights. To secure his immediate release without a conviction on his record, he accepted a non-custodial probation plea deal for lesser charges and was released in March 2024. Longest Awaiting Trial to an Acquittal: Condell Benyard (8 Years) If you require the trial process to end specifically in a not-guilty verdict (acquittal) rather than a hung jury or a plea deal, the record belongs to Jimmerson's co-defendant, Condell Benyard. The Timeline. Benyard was arrested alongside Jimmerson in May 2013. The Outcome. He remained locked in the exact same Georgia jail without a conviction until his case finally went to a jury in July 2023. The jury found him not guilty on all counts, ending his 8-year pretrial detention with a total, unblemished acquittal. Lee County, North Carolina, may soon strip this Georgia jail of its infamous title. The Allen case, with its growing record of alleged corruption, collusion, conspiracy, and cronyism, is rapidly becoming a case study in institutional failure.
keywords: How Long Can the Justice System Disrupt the Life of an Innocent Man?

records.section: 9. The Falsely Accused as a Constructed Defendant vs. the Record as the Actual Story
records.text: 9. The Falsely Accused as a Constructed Defendant vs. the Record as the Actual Story The version of Benjamin Allen presented by the prosecution is a construction. It is assembled from recast witness statements, selectively admitted exhibits, a narrative of darkness and predation that does not survive contact with the actual conditions of the night, and an aggravating factor that hardened over years of testimony evolution rather than appearing in the original record. That constructed version is not the record. The record tells a different story. The Constructed Version A predator who approached Deal at a bar, held a position of trust over her, and assaulted her when she was vulnerable. A flight in complete darkness, through woods and briars, by a frightened woman escaping an assailant. A scene from which evidence was destroyed rather than preserved. Witnesses who confirmed the complainant's account and supported the investigation's findings. A prosecution that responded proportionately to a credible, supported allegation. What the Record Actually Shows Deal initiated contact with Allen at the bar, followed him after he walked away, and voluntarily accompanied his group — all visible on video. The escape narrative describes terrain that does not exist in the direction Deal claimed to have run. The night had approximately 70% lunar illumination, making the "complete darkness" claim scientifically unsupported. The lead investigator had an undisclosed familial relationship with the key witness whose initial statement was exculpatory and was then recast. Two material witnesses who could have corroborated or undermined the account were never interviewed. A $150,000 extortion demand from Deal's social circle preceded the formal allegation and was not investigated. The prosecution's signature exhibit was conditionally admitted subject to a foundation requirement the State did not satisfy. The aggravating factor that elevated the charge evolved over years of testimonial development rather than appearing in the original record. The record does not tell the story of a guilty man who was processed by a just system. It tells the story of a man who was constructed as guilty — through selective handling of evidence, institutional conflicts, and narrative evolution — in a system that was oriented from the outset toward conviction rather than truth. The purpose of this archive is to make the actual record visible, so that the construction can be seen for what it is.

records.text: Edifice of Lies Project Map Evidence Viewer Case Record Timeline Players Scene Analysis Evidence Documents Analysis Contradictions 40 Impeachment Cards Deal's Ever Changing Testimony New Face General Videos Inspired Digital Media Case Study Data Snapshot Diagrams Connections False Story Mindmaps Accountability Misconduct Prosecutor Conduct Judicial Duty System Essay Search Soundtrack Case Study: State v. Benjamin Allen A military veteran and father was accused of sexual assault in Lee County, North Carolina, in October 2019. The prosecution that followed lasted more than six years. This page documents what the record shows and how the case continued despite evidence that contradicted the charge at every structural level. Profiles of the people involved are on the Players page. ⚠ 104 Distinct Violations ✔ 12‑0 Unanimous Acquittal First-Degree Forcible Rape ⏱ 38 Min Available Window vs. 48 min required 📂 37 State Continuances Attrition Strategy On this page ➜ Timeline of Impossibility ➜ Digital Disproof ➜ Forensic Analysis 1. The Initial Complaint 2. The Investigation Record 3. The Charging Decision 4. Pressure Dynamics 5. Evidence Against the Narrative 6. The Arc of Prosecution 7. Downstream Harms 8. Comparison to Base Rates Other pretrial detentions 9. The Constructed Defendant Related Sources Key Players ↗ Timeline of Impossibility The departure from Schooly’s bar was marked by a fundamental contradiction between witness testimony and the objective surveillance record. Lauren Deal’s sworn testimony portrayed the departure as a coordinated group event designed to establish the State’s “position of trust” theory. The video evidence shows otherwise: they did not leave together. That single fact renders this portion of her testimony highly suspect, and the problems compound from there across every time anchor that follows. State’s Theory Group of four (Deal, Allen, DeMarco, Happel) remained together at closing and departed together in Allen's white truck. Deal was comfortably familiar with the vehicle and the group. The departure served as the foundation for the “position of trust” aggravator. The testimony given to support this false narrative is as manufactured as the aggravating factor the ADA improperly applied to the charge. Video Reality The surveillance footage shows they did not leave together — departures occurred at separate times. Because Deal left the bar independently, the alleged joint-departure conversation about DeMarco driving and whose truck it was could not have taken place as described. Carmen Love also confirmed to Detective Freeman that the evening did not unfold the way Deal described to law enforcement but later changed her story when she was informed what the narrative would be for that evening. ⚖ Prosecution Exchange — Trial Transcript MS. BARTHOLOMEW: “Did you ever fall down while you were at Schooly’s? And when it became time to leave with Ben, Joseph, and Steve, what type of vehicle did you guys get into?” LAUREN DEAL: “A white lifted truck.” MS. BARTHOLOMEW: “How do you know it was Ben’s truck?” LAUREN DEAL: “I had seen it before, and he made the comment on the way out that Jay was going to drive his truck because he was the least intoxicated of all of us.” The truck was stock — not lifted. The “prior familiarity” claim is inconsistent with a timeline showing no meaningful contact for years. The designated-driver arrangement was Allen’s, made before Deal arrived; he did not describe DeMarco as “least intoxicated.” The detail in the complete fabrication here is striking. The video shows Deal leaving separately. There is no disputing that fact. There isn't even a close following of individual that could have led her to be mistaken. It is just entirely made up to push a narative. ⏰ Video-Confirmed & Documented Time Anchors (After hours of video that directly contradicts the evening described by Lauren Deal) ~2:00 AM Bar closes; lights on. Deal testified the group was together at this point. 2:04 AM DeMarco seen on video retrieving sandals at Schooly’s (objective video anchor). 2:25–2:35 AM Group estimated to arrive at Allen’s residence, based on ~15-minute drive time. ~2:40 AM Estimated exit — if Happel’s “less than five minutes” window is accepted at face value. 3:42 AM Deal arrives at CCH — State’s Exhibit 1 Video (objective anchor). 5:23 AM Chapel Hill intake paperwork. Teresa Deal testified the drive took approximately 45 minutes. The Five-Minute Impossibility Happel placed the entire period from entry to exit at less than five minutes . Within that window, the State’s account requires all of the following to have occurred: Entering the house and unlocking the door Using the bathroom Redressing after bathroom use An alleged push onto a 36-inch-high bed A one-handed overhead restraint of a resisting adult Removal of clothing from two adults The assault itself Escape from the residence That sequence is not merely tight. It is facially implausible. The Escape Narrative — Terrain & Light Claimed Ran hysterically through dense woods in pitch-black darkness for nearly an hour, sustaining briar cuts. No pants, no shoes. Screamed that Allen was “the devil” and that Happel and DeMarco “work for him.” Contradicted by the Record The route she identified leads onto an open airfield , not dense forest. No briars exist along that path; her cuts do not resemble briar injuries. Astronomical data: approximately 70% lunar illumination that night — directly contradicts the claim she could not see her hand in front of her face. DeMarco said he saw her running through a field . Deal said she was hiding behind a tree . The witnesses contradict each other as to her location. The direction she claimed to have run was the opposite direction of the road she said she ran toward and claimed she was located on 🧠 Interactive Mindmap: Explore the complete branch structure in Deconstructing the Lauren Deal Narrative to examine environmental conditions, terrain contradictions, and physiological implausibility. ⚠ Unaccounted Time: Three Irreconcilable Gaps Gap 1 — Exit to CCH ∼62 min From ∼2:40 AM exit to 3:42 AM CCH arrival. DeMarco and Happel claimed they searched only five minutes before DeMarco drove off. Where were Deal and DeMarco for the rest of the hour? Her visible impairment, her obesity, lack of physical fitness, and lack of footwear make a prolonged solo run implausible. Gap 2 — CCH to Chapel Hill ∼56 min unaccounted CCH arrival 3:42 AM. Chapel Hill intake 5:23 AM. Teresa Deal testified the drive took ∼45 minutes — accounting for 45 of 101 elapsed minutes. The remaining 56 minutes at CCH are unexplained. No CCH report to law enforcement has been produced, as would be required in a sexual assault case. Gap 3 — The Girlfriend Problem 45+ min round trip DeMarco called his girlfriend in Fayetteville. Deal was later wearing the sweatpants the girlfriend brought to CCH. The drive from Fayetteville alone takes at least 45 minutes . The claim that they arrived at CCH and immediately turned around for Chapel Hill cannot be true. State’s “Position of Trust” Theory vs. Surveillance Record State’s Claim Allen occupied a position of trust that he exploited to lure Deal—evidenced by her recognizing his truck from previous occasions, greeting him with a hug, and entrusting him with her keys. Implied Warrant A woman who hands over her keys and joins a familiar male friend’s group for a social gathering acts under the umbrella of established trust, which can constitute a statutory aggravator. Video Disproof Allen refused the keys ; Deal handed them to DeMarco — a man she had never met. Deal’s friends left earlier. She eventually left the bar alone after multiple failed attempts to get Allen’s attention. It was not a smooth group departure. The State needed that cohesion because it was the social glue for the “lure” theory. Pattern: Narrative Manufacture The account of who remained at the bar, who left with whom, how the truck was identified, why DeMarco drove, how intoxicated Deal was, and what happened after leaving the residence seriously conflicts with the video, timelines, terrain, and common sense. None of this appears ambiguous. Much of it is directly testable. Deal’s trial testimony diverged sharply from her earlier statements. The later testimony became cleaner, more element-driven, and more useful to the prosecution. That pattern does not look like natural memory development. When the polished version directly conflicts with objective video evidence, the problem is no longer mere inconsistency — it becomes evidence of narrative manufacture . Carmen Love told Freeman that the evening did not unfold as Deal described to law enforcement. Rather than preserving those contradictions, he altered the official narrative to bury them. Digital Disproof: The Bar Surveillance The State’s “Position of Trust” aggravator was built entirely on sworn testimony about a friendly social evening. Objective surveillance video from Schooly’s refutes each key claim. Tap any card to reveal what the footage actually shows. Sworn Testimony 🗣 “Initial Hug” “I ran up and hugged him.” Tap to reveal video reality ↻ Objective Reality 📹 Avoidance No hug occurred upon arrival. Deal is clearly seen avoiding Allen's proximity on the footage. Perjury Sworn Testimony 🗣 “Group Drinking” “We sat and drank for hours as a group with Carmen and Peter.” Tap to reveal video reality ↻ Objective Reality 📹 Timeline Fraud Peter West left at 11:32 PM; Carmen Love left at 12:41 AM. Deal did not interact with Allen until after Carmen Love left at 12:41 a.m. Timeline Fabrication Sworn Testimony 🗣 “The Key Transfer” “I threw him my keys because I trusted him.” Tap to reveal video reality ↻ Objective Reality 📹 Refusal Allen explicitly refused the keys. Deal subsequently handed them to Joseph DeMarco instead. Rebuttal of Trust Aggravator Freeman Affidavit 📄 The 2:00 AM Conversation Freeman swore Deal told Carmen Love at 2:00 AM she was leaving with Allen. Tap to reveal video reality ↻ Objective Reality 📹 Impossible Security footage confirms Carmen Love exited Schooly's at exactly 12:41:25 AM — over an hour before the claimed conversation. Franks Violation Forensic & Anatomical Disproof The ADA’s representations during plea negotiations directly contradicted laboratory and medical records. The alleged assault mechanics are additionally excluded by the defendant’s documented physical impairments. 🧬 The DNA Misrepresentation The ADA's Representation During plea talks, ADA Bartholomew stated: "We found your sperm and DNA on her." SBI Report (05/11/2020) “No spermatozoa present.” Y-STR Reality The lab found a non-individualizing profile matching 1 in 518 Caucasian males, including all paternal relatives. The sample was subsequently consumed without a notice of defense. 🩺 SANE & Biomechanical Analysis 0 FLACC Pain Score None Genital Trauma / Bruising The Anatomical Fantasy The Claim: Defendant held both wrists above her head with one hand while simultaneously removing fitted leggings from a 200lb adult. The Reality: Allen sustained a 2005 fracture resulting in zero grip strength in his left hand. Geometrically, a body positioned for penetration physically blocks the downward removal path of pants. 1. The Initial Complaint: What Was Alleged, When, and to Whom The complaint arose from events at Schooly’s bar in Lee County, North Carolina, in the early hours of October 19, 2019, and the hours that followed. The sequence below draws on the documentary record, testimony, and video evidence now available in this archive. The Bar — Evening of October 18 into October 19, 2019 Lauren Deal and her group arrived at Goodfellas around 6:30 p.m. on October 18, 2019, and at Schooly’s around 9:30 p.m. Benjamin Allen and his group arrived at Schooly’s at approximately 12:08 a.m. on October 19. The bar video is part of this archive. That video shows Deal's group and Allen's group present simultaneously. It also shows specific interactions — including Deal initiating contact with Allen, attempting to introduce him to others, and following him after he walked away — that directly contradict key elements of the later complaint. The Allegation Deal alleged that Allen sexually assaulted her after she accompanied him from the bar. She alleged she escaped by running through pitch-black darkness and briars, hid behind trees, and was eventually spotted from the road by Joe DeMarco, who picked her up. She described the environment as “complete darkness” yet still identified vehicle types, recognized DeMarco by sight, and maintained eye contact as she approached his vehicle. First Report — Officer Isaac Haines Officer Haines conducted the first institutional interview with Deal. He testified that his role was preliminary fact-finding to determine whether the matter warranted a detective assignment. This framing creates a timing problem: Freeman testified that he had already been notified about a sexual assault allegation before the Haines interview was complete, suggesting the matter was escalated to detective-level investigation before the threshold predicate had been established. Haines described the investigative mission as proving Allen guilty, not determining whether the allegation was credible. Haines was subsequently promoted to Detective following this case. 2. The Investigation Record: What Was Collected vs. What Was Ignored An investigation's integrity is measured not only by what it found but by what it chose not to look for. The omissions in this record are not minor. They are structural — the materials most likely to undermine the complaint are precisely the materials that were handled selectively or not at all. Collected Bar Video Footage Video from Schooly’s was collected. The footage documents Deal’s behavior and interactions that evening, including moments when Deal initiates contact with Allen—contradicting her later account—and shows Carmen Love and James Morrison leaving together without speaking to Allen or his friends, directly undermining the social context the investigation’s narrative claims. Not Collected / Not Used Statements from Material Witnesses James Morrison and Peter West III — both present at the bar and part of Deal’s extended social group — were never interviewed. Morrison was Carmen Love’s boyfriend. West’s father was a Sheriff’s Office employee who signed Allen’s jail release. The record provides no explanation for why two identified witnesses who were present for the relevant events were never contacted. Distorted Carmen Love's Initial Statement Love’s first recorded statement to Freeman — her own family member — did not identify Allen by name and did not supply the incriminating detail later attributed to it. Freeman subsequently recast that statement in official documents. Because the original recording exists and the defense can access it, the alteration is directly comparable and provable. Freeman claimed to have used Love’s statement as a basis for probable cause even though its actual content did not support that use. Uninvestigated The $150,000 Extortion Demand A $150,000 extortion demand connected to Joel Kelly preceded or accompanied the formal accusation. Kelly’s daughter was Deal’s best friend; Deal’s other best friend worked for Kelly. The investigation did not adequately explore the financial motive and social architecture of the extortion—a gap that would be highly relevant to any credibility assessment of the complainant’s motive. Manufactured Evidence Destruction Innuendo Freeman later suggested that cleanup behavior at Allen’s residence was consistent with evidence destruction—without processing the scene in any way that would establish what evidence existed there, where it was located, or whether anything had been removed. The insinuation extended to a different room from the one where the assault was allegedly committed. This is the investigative equivalent of creating a negative implication from the absence of something the investigation never actually looked for. Chronological Defect The Assignment Timing Problem The testimonial record indicates that Freeman was already aware of and involved in the case before Haines's preliminary interview was complete. If Haines's stated role was to determine whether a detective was needed, then Freeman's prior notification is a structural impossibility unless the escalation decision had been made before any factual basis for it existed. This creates a Franks v. Delaware concern: the chronology underlying the probable cause affidavit may be materially false. 3. The Charging Decision A charging decision carries legal and moral weight. It requires a genuine assessment of whether the available evidence, taken at its strongest, could support a conviction before a fair finder of fact. The materials in this archive raise serious questions about whether this assessment was ever conducted honestly. What Existed at the Time of Charging A complainant whose account included physical impossibilities contradicted by terrain, lighting conditions, and recorded video. Bar video showing Deal initiating contact with Allen, tracking him after he walked away, and voluntarily accompanying his group. An initial witness statement (Carmen Love) that was exculpatory in its original form. An investigator with an undisclosed familial relationship to a key witness. Two identified material witnesses who had never been interviewed. An unexplained extortion demand in the same social circle as the complainant. A chronological impossibility in the escalation timeline that should have triggered review of the probable cause affidavit but no probable cause affidavit exist even after almost seven years. What the Decision Required The decision to charge over these materials required either that the prosecutor had not reviewed them, had reviewed them and concluded they were immaterial, or had reviewed them and concluded that conviction was achievable regardless of what they showed. The prosecution's subsequent conduct —including the handling of Exhibit 4, the aggravating-factor construction, and indicators of witness coaching — points to the third possibility. 4. Pressure Dynamics: Family Connections to Law Enforcement and Local DA Relationships The structural environment surrounding this case was not neutral. The record documents a set of relationships between the complainant’s social circle and law enforcement personnel that, taken together, explain how a case with this evidentiary profile was treated as credible, why certain witnesses disappeared from the record, and how the language attributed to insiders ("it didn’t matter whether Mr. Allen was innocent") reflects something more than personal bias. Freeman ↔ Carmen Love The lead investigator had a familial relationship with the key witness whose initial statement was exculpatory. The investigator recast Love’s statement rather than preserving it. This conflict was not disclosed. Under basic due process principles, an investigator with a family relationship to a witness cannot be treated as neutral when the question is whether that witness’s account corroborates or undermines the charge. Freeman ↔ James Morrison Morrison was Love’s boyfriend — and therefore connected to Freeman through Love. He was at the bar, and his non-interview is unexplained. Failing to interview him fits the broader pattern: the record excluded every uncontrolled witness who could have provided an independent account of Deal’s behavior that evening. Peter West III ↔ Sheriff's Office West was present at the bar. His father worked at the Sheriff’s Office and personally signed Allen’s jail release. West was never interviewed. His institutional proximity and absence from the investigation suggest the investigation’s scope was shaped—not by the evidence—but by the social and professional networks within it. Jolynda Adcock's Statement Adcock's documented statement — "it didn't matter whether Mr. Allen was innocent" — is not merely an expression of personal hostility. It is a statement about perceived institutional power. It reflects the understanding, within the complainant's extended circle, that the Sheriff's Department relationships available to them were sufficient to make the outcome of the case independent of its factual merits. Haines's Promotion Officer Haines, the initial responding officer who described the investigative mission as proving Allen guilty rather than determining the truth of the allegation, was subsequently promoted to Detective. Whatever the formal basis for that promotion, its timing in this case's institutional record is documented here. The Extortion Network The $150,000 extortion demand, connected to Joel Kelly, whose daughter was Deal’s best friend and whose employee was Deal’s other best friend, was generated before or alongside the formal complaint. The failure to investigate this network as a source of motive — and the failure to trace its relationship to the timing and substance of the allegation — is a fundamental investigative omission. 5. Evidence That Contradicted the Narrative — and How It Was Handled The complaint's narrative is not merely weak at its edges. The core of it — the flight, the darkness, the geography — collapses under basic scrutiny. The following contradictions are documented in the record and cross-referenced in contradictions.html . The Darkness Claim vs. the Lunar Record Deal described running in "complete darkness." Photometric and radiometric data confirm approximately 70% lunar illumination (Waxing/Waning Gibbous) on the night in question. At this illumination level, a person with normal vision can detect large objects at distances exceeding 50 feet, recognize body silhouettes and movement, and navigate open terrain without artificial light. Deal simultaneously claimed "complete darkness" while identifying that an approaching vehicle was not Allen's large truck, recognizing DeMarco as the driver, establishing eye contact with him, and making a deliberate decision to approach. The word "darkness" is invoked selectively: it appears to explain disorientation and disappears when recognition, identification, and volitional conduct need to be established. The Geographic Impossibility Deal claimed to have run through woods and briars in the direction away from the house before reaching a road near Route 1. The direction she described leads to a large, flat, open airfield — not woods, not briars, not concealed terrain. There is no dense undergrowth in that direction. The airfield is open and visible. To reach the road near Route 1, she would have had to reverse course and run back toward the house. The investigation did not engage with this geographic contradiction. The terrain has been documented in the scene archive at scene.html . The Video Record vs. the Social Context Claimed Bar video shows Carmen Love and James Morrison departing Schooly's at approximately 12:41 AM — without having spoken to Allen or his group. Deal's account implied a different social context within the bar. The video shows Deal initiating contact with Allen, attempting to introduce him to others, and following him after he walked away. The video does not show a reluctant or passive witness. It shows voluntary engagement. That footage is timestamped and available in the archive. DeMarco's Statement vs. Deal's Trial Testimony Joe DeMarco told Freeman he saw Deal "running through a field near Route 1" while driving. Deal's trial testimony described running through pitch-black woods in a different direction. These accounts are not in minor tension — they describe different physical scenarios in different locations under different conditions. DeMarco's account was inaccurate from the beginning as he was afraid of getting accused of something by Deal so he went along with making up a story. His account was changed in Freeman's search warrant affidavit and retellings. Deal's trial account does not align with the geography and lighting conditions. Exhibit 4: The Facebook Messages Facebook messages identified as Exhibit 4 were presented without device metadata, custodial proof, or foundation sufficient to resolve attribution — particularly where later screenshots identified a different user of the same phone. The court conditionally admitted the exhibit subject to the State's obligation to link it to a prior conversation that would provide context. That condition was not meaningfully satisfied. Only the first screenshot was emphasized; subsequent screenshots identifying another phone user were withheld from the jury's view, in apparent violation of N.C. R. Evid. 106. How Contradictory Evidence Was Handled The documentary record reflects a consistent pattern: evidence that undermined the narrative was either ignored (Morrison, West), recast (Love's initial statement), managed selectively (Exhibit 4's full screenshot sequence), or met with insinuation rather than proof (the cleanup/destruction-of-evidence narrative). The pattern is too consistent to be explained by inadvertence. Each handling decision was in a direction that favored conviction. 6. The Arc of the 6+ Year Prosecution The prosecution of Benjamin Allen extended more than six years from the date of the alleged offense in October 2019. That duration is not simply a product of court congestion or procedural complexity. It reflects a sequence of decisions that prolonged exposure to prosecution for a defendant whose record contained, from the outset, materials that should have triggered review. Initial Arrest and Charge Allen was arrested and charged with sexual assault following the investigation led by Detective Freeman. The arrest took place despite the evidentiary defects described in this record: an uninvestigated extortion demand, an exculpatory witness statement that had been recast, two uninterviewed material witnesses, and a probable cause chronology that did not hold together. Continuances and Delay The case proceeded through hearings, continuances, and pretrial motions over an extended period. Each continuance that moved the trial date further into the future extended Allen's period of legal jeopardy — with consequences for employment, housing, family access, and health documented in the downstream harms section below. The full docket record is available in the document archive. Motions Practice Pretrial motions raised issues including Brady violations, the chronological defect in the probable cause affidavit (implicating Franks v. Delaware ), and evidentiary handling failures. The Exhibit 4 conditional admission ruling, in which the court required the State to link the exhibit to a prior conversation before relying on it, is a documented instance of the court placing conditions on the prosecution's evidence presentation — conditions the State then did not satisfy. Narrative Evolution as a Prosecution Tool Across the arc of the case, Deal's testimony evolved. The "position of trust" aggravating factor developed over time in ways inconsistent with the earliest statements and with the video record of Deal's behavior at the bar. That evolution — from a social encounter at a bar where Deal initiated contact, to a story in which Allen held a position of trust over Deal — required the original record to be progressively buried rather than resolved. The more the narrative evolved, the weaker its connection to the documented facts became. 7. Downstream Harms A prosecution does not exist only in courtrooms. It exists in every part of a person's life from the day of arrest forward. The following categories of harm document what a false accusation that proceeds for more than six years actually costs — not as a hypothetical, but as a record of documented consequence. Employment Career Destruction Allen lost employment as a direct consequence of the accusation and the protracted prosecution. Military service and the vocational record built before the accusation were effectively severed. Re-employment becomes structurally difficult for a defendant whose status remains unresolved across years of hearings and continuances. Housing Housing Instability Loss of employment and the financial burden of legal defense across more than six years produces housing instability. A defendant cannot plan housing, financing, or community stability when their legal status remains unresolved—with each continuance extending the period of uncertainty. Family Separation from Family Allen is a father. An accusation of this nature and duration does not only restrict the accused's freedom — it disrupts parental access, creates conditions for protective orders, and forces children to grow up with a parent under prosecution. That harm is not reversible by acquittal. Finances Legal and Financial Cost Defending a felony-level sexual assault case over six or more years — through motions, hearings, trial preparation, and any appellate proceedings — produces a financial cost that exceeds the resources of most individuals. That cost is borne entirely by the defendant while the State prosecutes with public resources. Health Physical and Psychological Toll Six years of pending felony prosecution — with its associated uncertainty, financial stress, social stigma, family disruption, and public record — produces documented psychological harm. For a military veteran who has already navigated service-related stress, the compounding effect of a fabricated accusation and institutional pursuit is not a marginal addition to a normal life. It is a consuming structural experience. Reputation The Public Record Problem An arrest and charge for sexual assault creates a public record. That record exists independent of outcome. Where the prosecution is false — built on a recast witness statement, uninvestigated exculpatory evidence, and a complainant whose account is physically impossible — the reputational harm is not a byproduct of a fair system. It is a harm produced by the system's failure. 8. Comparison to Base Rates The question of how rare it is for a case with this evidentiary profile to proceed this far is not an idle one. Base rate data on false accusation rates, prosecution rates conditional on evidence quality, and case duration data provide the population-level context against which this record should be evaluated. The Evidence Profile of This Case Bar video directly contradicting the complainant's account of the social interaction. Documented physical impossibilities in the escape narrative (terrain, lighting, direction). An exculpatory witness statement that was altered rather than preserved. Two identified material witnesses who were never interviewed. An undisclosed conflict of interest in the lead investigator. A financial motive (extortion) that was not investigated. A probable cause chronology that contained a structural impossibility. A prosecution's evidence handling that violated multiple evidentiary rules. What Base Rates Suggest Research on sexual assault prosecution — including work by the National Registry of Exonerations and academic studies of prosecutorial screening — consistently finds that cases with exculpatory video evidence, physical impossibilities in the complainant's narrative, and undisclosed investigator conflicts rarely proceed past initial screening where those materials are meaningfully engaged. Cases in which those materials are present but suppressed, recast, or ignored present a different pattern: the materials that should have stopped the case become invisible to the decision-makers downstream, and the case proceeds on the momentum of the charge rather than the merits of the record. A 6+ year prosecution in the face of this evidentiary profile is an outlier. It is not explained by case complexity. It is explained by the structural dynamics documented in this archive: investigator conflicts, selective witness handling, and a complaint embedded in a network with direct access to law enforcement. The Research Context False allegation rates in sexual assault cases are contested in the academic literature, with credible estimates ranging from approximately 2% to 10% of reported cases depending on methodology. What is less contested is that the subset of false allegations that result in charges, trial, and multi-year prosecution represent a small fraction of even those cases. For a case with documented exculpatory video, physical geography inconsistencies, an uninvestigated financial motive, and an investigator conflict to reach trial — and proceed past trial — places this matter in the extreme tail of that already-small population. The data snapshot page provides additional context on these figures. How Long Can the Justice System Disrupt the Life of an Innocent Man? Two men, one Georgia jail, and more than a decade without a conviction. The Maurice Jimmerson Case (10 Years, 10 Months) The Arrest. Maurice Jimmerson was arrested in Dougherty County, Georgia, in May 2013 on murder charges. The Stagnation. He was held continuously in a local jail awaiting his day in court. His case was delayed for nearly eleven years due to systemic bureaucratic failures, a courthouse flood, the COVID-19 pandemic, and an eight-month stretch where the court completely forgot to assign him an attorney. The Zero-Conviction Conclusion. He finally went to trial in July 2023, which resulted in a mistrial (hung jury) rather than a conviction. Because he had spent over a decade locked up as a legally innocent man, his defense attorney successfully argued that a retrial would heavily violate his Sixth Amendment rights. To secure his immediate release without a conviction on his record, he accepted a non-custodial probation plea deal for lesser charges and was released in March 2024. Longest Awaiting Trial to an Acquittal: Condell Benyard (8 Years) If you require the trial process to end specifically in a not-guilty verdict (acquittal) rather than a hung jury or a plea deal, the record belongs to Jimmerson's co-defendant, Condell Benyard. The Timeline. Benyard was arrested alongside Jimmerson in May 2013. The Outcome. He remained locked in the exact same Georgia jail without a conviction until his case finally went to a jury in July 2023. The jury found him not guilty on all counts, ending his 8-year pretrial detention with a total, unblemished acquittal. Lee County, North Carolina, may soon strip this Georgia jail of its infamous title. The Allen case, with its growing record of alleged corruption, collusion, conspiracy, and cronyism, is rapidly becoming a case study in institutional failure. 9. The Falsely Accused as a Constructed Defendant vs. the Record as the Actual Story The version of Benjamin Allen presented by the prosecution is a construction. It is assembled from recast witness statements, selectively admitted exhibits, a narrative of darkness and predation that does not survive contact with the actual conditions of the night, and an aggravating factor that hardened over years of testimony evolution rather than appearing in the original record. That constructed version is not the record. The record tells a different story. The Constructed Version A predator who approached Deal at a bar, held a position of trust over her, and assaulted her when she was vulnerable. A flight in complete darkness, through woods and briars, by a frightened woman escaping an assailant. A scene from which evidence was destroyed rather than preserved. Witnesses who confirmed the complainant's account and supported the investigation's findings. A prosecution that responded proportionately to a credible, supported allegation. What the Record Actually Shows Deal initiated contact with Allen at the bar, followed him after he walked away, and voluntarily accompanied his group — all visible on video. The escape narrative describes terrain that does not exist in the direction Deal claimed to have run. The night had approximately 70% lunar illumination, making the "complete darkness" claim scientifically unsupported. The lead investigator had an undisclosed familial relationship with the key witness whose initial statement was exculpatory and was then recast. Two material witnesses who could have corroborated or undermined the account were never interviewed. A $150,000 extortion demand from Deal's social circle preceded the formal allegation and was not investigated. The prosecution's signature exhibit was conditionally admitted subject to a foundation requirement the State did not satisfy. The aggravating factor that elevated the charge evolved over years of testimonial development rather than appearing in the original record. The record does not tell the story of a guilty man who was processed by a just system. It tells the story of a man who was constructed as guilty — through selective handling of evidence, institutional conflicts, and narrative evolution — in a system that was oriented from the outset toward conviction rather than truth. The purpose of this archive is to make the actual record visible, so that the construction can be seen for what it is.
